title: THE QUIET SCHOOL OF HIGH WENDEL
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE MAN WHO WAS THE ELEVATOR
candidates.premise: Harrow Tower has fourteen storeys and sixty-one households, the oldest of them on the top floors. On the third night of a heat wave the lift stops between the seventh and eighth floors with a diabetic grandmother inside, and the tenants' association and the superintendent, Dov Lindqvist, who have not spoken civilly since the rent strike, shout across the lobby about who locked the machine room. Illuminara can carry people down the stairwell, but forty frightened elderly residents will not be carried by a stranger, and she cannot make an absent landlord replace a motor.

candidates.title: THE QUIET SCHOOL OF HIGH WENDEL
candidates.premise: In the mountain town of High Wendel, nine hundred people speak Wenn, a tone language in which one syllable means river, sorrow or yes by pitch alone. Since the new cable car opened in spring, forty children under nine have stopped speaking at school. The clinic calls it shared trauma, the school board wants the children moved down the valley for therapy, and the cable-car engineer, Ines Kallas, whose project ended the town's winter isolation, insists her machine is silent. Illuminara can listen better than any clinician, but she cannot know what a child chooses not to say.

candidates.title: THE CITY THAT BREATHED IN TURNS
candidates.premise: Under the dome of Marrow Deep thirty thousand people share air for half that number, so for three generations the city has lived in shifts: a Day Watch and a Night Watch alternate sleep and work, each with its own councils, marriages, holidays and grandmothers. A visiting engineer, Kiran Abel, has found a way to double the air supply, and the Night Watch's warden, Hedda Vandermeer, has locked him out of the plant, because the fix would end the shifts and with them the two halves of the city. Illuminara can hold a failing seal, but she cannot make either half believe the other's grandmother mattered.

candidates.title: THE WEDDING TWO CALENDARS FORBADE
candidates.premise: Between the neighbouring worlds of Oste and Quill a wedding has been arranged that both peoples call the end of a century of quarrels. Oste marries at the false dawn and keeps that day sacred to the dead; Quill mourns on exactly that day and marries only at the full year-turn that Oste regards as unlucky. Both grandmothers have vetoed every compromise, the couple are about to elope, and a trade pact worth eight million jobs hangs on the ceremony. Illuminara can shelter the hall, but she cannot unite two calendars.

candidates.title: THE LOTTERY THAT NINETY WORLDS TRUSTED
candidates.premise: Every settlement right in the Cinder Arm is awarded by a drawing from the Allotter, a thousand-year-old machine whose source of chance is sealed inside it and whose only guardian is the hereditary Keeper, Odalys Brandt. A prefect of the losing worlds, Ioana Reyes, has produced a statistical anomaly she says proves rigging, and ninety worlds that have not fought in nine centuries are mobilising. Opening the Allotter would destroy it, and with it the reason ninety worlds accept their luck. Illuminara can sit between the two women, but she cannot prove a machine fair by saying so.

candidates.title: THE ARBITER AT THE CROSSROADS OF UNIVERSES
candidates.premise: A junction between universes is held by the Arbiter, an ancient presence that lets travellers through only after taking from each the one thing they would most grieve to lose. The people of a collapsing world, forty thousand of them, have reached it, and the first families who paid the toll arrive on the far side hollowed, their memories of their children gone. The refugees' leaders want to storm the crossing. Illuminara can walk through unharmed, but she cannot pay for forty thousand, and she cannot out-bargain a being that knows what each of them values.

candidates.title: THE SHADE THAT WOULD NOT MOVE
candidates.premise: An orbital sunshade built to cool the continent of Tarsa has stalled over one growing region for thirty-four days, and three hundred million people have six weeks of dusk-light before the harvest fails. Its twelve-person crew, under Commander Beatrix Salcedo, will not move it, because a charter written after an old accident forbids repositioning under load and a single burn would also drop a field of debris. Illuminara can shield a small region from falling debris, but not a continent.

candidates.title: THE CHILD BOTH MOTHERS HAD CARRIED
candidates.premise: Seven-year-old Pim was carried by a human surrogate, Marit Aldous, from an egg of the Hesh, a people whose mothers carry the mother-name and the child into the world together. Her genetic mother, Ulenne, has crossed a light-year to take her home, and Marit has locked the door. Both have lawyers, neither will move, and the child has stopped eating. Illuminara can shelter a conversation, but she cannot make anyone love in a way they do not.

candidates.title: THE QUARANTINE THAT PROTECTED THE WRONG PEOPLE
candidates.premise: The port world of Anvil Reach has closed its gates to a plague-stricken moon, and its Health Minister, Lucan Rho, is praised for it. But the dockworkers who unload the cargo that is still allowed through, many of them living in the port's lower terraces, are falling ill at three times anyone else's rate, while the Minister's own model says the quarantine is working. Illuminara can reach every terrace, but she cannot see a disease she has no sample of.

candidates.title: THE VILLAGE THAT STOPPED ARGUING
candidates.premise: After Illuminara holds back a flood at Ketterby for one night, the village makes her its patron. By spring the irrigation council has stopped meeting, the dam's repairs wait for her, and she has begun to enjoy being the person whose arrival ends a quarrel. When the sluice gate fails while she is away, a village that has forgotten how to decide for itself must choose between two plans in a single day.

selection.title: THE QUIET SCHOOL OF HIGH WENDEL
selection.reason: The quietest candidate makes the strongest closing contrast and the clearest R14 demonstration that understanding changes intervention. The children are not symbols of silence and Ines is not a straw engineer: a cable car ended winter isolation, while a channel nobody measured may be corrupting children's speech. Illuminara succeeds only by becoming a fallible student, letting a six-year-old correct her tone, and helping sceptics run a test they can inspect. The positive result preserves both the town's link and its language, while the children retain the choice and timing of speech and two may remain quiet for months.
selection.risk: The acoustic explanation can be physically vague or medically overconfident, and a single recording must not erase trauma, hearing conditions or the clinician's legitimate duty. The author should specify a reproducible hum or harmonic band, compare the same syllables with the drive on and off, include adult and child controls, and preregister what change would count as masking before anyone hears the answer. Dr Orsolya should help rule out alternatives and protect children rather than be humiliated. Ines must identify a bounded retuning or damping change, independently verify it, and keep authority to stop an unsafe modification. No child should be required to speak as proof of the adults' theory.

First draft of S3 from C02, following B01 and S2 close. B01 risk handled: the acoustic claim is made reproducible and falsifiable before anyone hears a word. A card signed by Illuminara, Ines and Dr Orsolya fixes the pass criterion in advance (drive running: more than 3 of 12 children's recordings misheard, drive stopped: at most 1, adults correct both times). The same recordings are played with the drive running and stopped, with adult controls, in randomised order, to a panel of eight who write slips. Ines runs her own sweep on her own instrument and keeps authority over tension, brake and rope; she limits her change to isolation mount, casing absorber and a four percent speed reduction (about a minute and a half on a 38 minute ride), and a valley inspector verifies the result independently. Dr Orsolya is not humiliated: he names what would change his mind, withdraws only the transfer, keeps fear open as a live hypothesis and takes the two children (Wilma, Teo) who are still quiet. No child is asked to speak as proof; Nessa's one recording is played with her own permission. The discovery that changes the intervention (R14): Illuminara first turns her hearing down to a teacher's range and is herself misheard by the channel, then is corrected by a six-year-old (yes is a little hill, not a mountain); she is a bad student before she is a diagnostician. Love in action: a whole school day spent asking the children for nothing; consent asked before every recording; Ines's pride respected by letting her measure with her own instrument; the board's dissent kept. Outcome (3a): 38 of 40 speaking within three weeks, transfer shelved, the cable car kept with a measured change, two children still supported by the clinician. A warm, unusually coherent first draft that fulfils the selected premise without turning the engineer, physician or children into symbols. Illuminara becomes a fallible listener before she becomes a diagnostician; Nessa's little-hill correction changes the intervention; Ines demands an inspectable test; Orsolya preserves fear as a live alternative; and the ending gives speech, continued silence and clinical care equal dignity. Three causal joints need revision before final: Orsolya's present transfer recommendation is too coercive and under-worked to preserve his legitimate duty, the pre-signed experiment does not define how eight listeners turn slips into a pass or protect against a visible fixed-order condition, and the overnight gearbox intervention is acoustically verified without an equally explicit safety commissioning check. {"rank":1,"point_id":"P1","area":"make Orsolya's clinical concern and the clinic pathway legitimate, specific and voluntary","evidence":"At the gate Sabrina says the children still talk at home, especially in back rooms, yet Orsolya moves directly from the shared silence to a board vote that would send forty children away for six weeks with family visits only on Sundays. The draft shows no hearing, neurological, speech-language or trauma assessment already performed, and his line that a silent child has 'lost a year of language' is too broad for children who retain home speech. S3 T03 revision. Addressed P1, P2 and P3 of the T02 critique and the shape note. Protected: Illuminara turning her hearing down and being mis-heard; Nessa's little hill and her authority; the ambient-tone mechanism and 'a peak is not a child'; the criterion signed before listening, matched adult controls, consent, Illuminara not voting; Ines keeping the machine, refusing tension, brake and rope and naming the four percent; Orsolya keeping fear alive and taking Wilma and Teo; the non-unanimous board and the final snow scene. Changes: scene 1 gives Orsolya what he has ruled out, the concrete harm (reading assessments), consent and assent, and his opposition to the board's wording; scene 4 defines the panel design and the item rule on the card, adds the reversed order and one sceptical exchange; scene 5 names Ines's stop conditions and adds a one-paragraph commissioning ending on Sabrina's bread; scene 6 keeps Dessau visible as an offer that one family looked at and declined. Scenes 2 and 3 are unchanged. Outcome (3a) unchanged: 38 of 40 speaking, transfer shelved, the cable car kept with a measured change and a safety check, two children cared for with a second cause. Costs: a minute and a half on the ride, two quiet children, two board members who think the doctor yielded too fast. R14 evidence on the page: the carrying scenes are the garden (a six-year-old corrects Illuminara) and the noon test (criterion signed before the result), and now the gate, where Orsolya's duty is stated before it is answered. To check: whether scene 4 now reads as a methods section, whether Orsolya's three long turns in scene 1 stall the gate, and whether scene 3 is still too expository (unchanged). Speaking roles: five (Illuminara, Sabrina, Dr Orsolya, Nessa, Ines).

The revision substantially succeeds. Orsolya now has a defensible clinical duty, opposes compulsory board wording before Illuminara proves the acoustic mechanism, and retains a voluntary specialist option afterward. The listening test now has an item rule and opposed orders, and Ines's repair is followed by independent commissioning rather than an acoustic result alone. The emotional and causal spine remains intact: Illuminara becomes a student of Nessa, evidence changes two responsible adults without humiliating them, and the ending protects both the thirty-eight children who speak and the two who do not. But neither the card nor narration states that the two four-person panels receive complementary twelve-recording sets. S3 T05 AUTHOR_FINAL. Only P1 and P2 of the T04 critique were changed; all other prose is identical to T03 (scenes 1-3 and 6 untouched). Scene 4: the card now states Set A/Set B allocation and the two panels' complementary order, the 'twenty minutes' rest has both rooms listening at once, and the order answer refers to panels. Scene 5: an overnight hold (last evening run until nine) named as an eleven-hour cost; times six to nine are the next morning. Shape line says 'a night of repair'. Outcome (3a) unchanged: transfer shelved, Dessau voluntary, car kept with measured acoustic gain and safety commissioning, thirty-eight children speaking, Wilma and Teo cared for. R14: understanding changes action (Illuminara lowers her hearing, accepts a six-year-old's correction, shares falsification authority); love is attention, consent, an inspectable test, a bounded repair and continuing care; no power decides the conflict.

The exact T05 final resolves both bounded points left by T04 without reopening the story's frame. The signed card now divides the twenty-four recordings into complementary A and B sets and assigns them to two four-person panels in opposed condition order, so every voice receives exactly four running-condition and four stopped-condition judgments while no listener hears a voice twice. The hall scene executes that assignment, preserves the three-of-four item rule and shows the same split in each panel. The repair is now an honestly priced overnight hold: the last evening run to nine in the morning, with sweeps at six, an empty run at seven, an emergency stop at eight and independently signed commissioning before the first loaded cabin at nine. These repairs preserve Nessa teaching Illuminara the small rising hill, Ines's intelligent resistance and engineering limits, Orsolya's duty and revision, the voluntary Dessau option, the thirty-eight children who resume speaking, and continuing care for Wilma and Teo. No further creative turn is justified.

final_critic_line: Illuminara learns from Nessa that the children are speaking clearly outside the school, then helps Ines and Dr Orsolya test the cable car's masking note under a signed, reconstructible protocol; Ines freely repairs the mechanism under independent safety commissioning, the board shelves compulsory transfer, thirty-eight children speak again, and the two whose silence has another root receive patient local care and a voluntary specialist option without being called failures.
